C'est l'expérience de Tversky et Kahnema: This is Tversky and Kahneman's 1974 experiment: with 10, the average estimate was 25%; with 65, 45%.
En 2006, Englich et Mussweiler montrent: In 2006, Englich and Mussweiler showed that even experienced legal professionals are anchored. Early studies had thought experts more resistant.
Huber, Payne et Puto décrivent ce leurre: Huber, Payne and Puto described this "asymmetrically dominated" decoy in 1982. Dan Ariely cites the real case of The Economist: nobody took the decoy offer, but removing it reversed the choices.
Tversky et Kahneman décrivent cette heur: Tversky and Kahneman described this heuristic in 1973: we judge an event more frequent when examples come easily to mind.
Tversky and Kahneman described this heuristic in 1973. Massive coverage of rare events makes them more present in the mind, and so more likely in our eyes.
C'est l'expérience de Tversky et Kahnema: This is Tversky and Kahneman's 1973 experiment: people think words starting with "k" are more common because they come to mind faster, whereas a typical text has twice as many with "k" as the third letter.
Une attaque de requin fait la une, la mo: A shark attack makes headlines, death by falling aircraft parts almost never. As a result, people overestimate the first risk and underestimate the second, as Tversky and Kahneman described in 1973.
Wald travaillait au Statistical Research: Wald worked at Columbia University's Statistical Research Group, which issued eight memoranda on analysing damaged combat aircraft. The planes hit in vital spots never came back to be counted.
En 1973, Kahneman et Tversky montrent qu: In 1973, Kahneman and Tversky showed that students ignore grade statistics as soon as a particular student is described to them: we judge by resemblance, not by frequency.
Kahneman introduit WYSIATI, « ce que tu: Kahneman introduced WYSIATI, "what you see is all there is", in Thinking, Fast and Slow, published in 2011, to explain overconfidence: the mind reasons with what it has and rarely accounts for what it lacks.
Darwin l'avait remarqué : « L'ignorance: Darwin had noticed it: "Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge." Kruger and Dunning received an Ig Nobel Prize for their paper in 2000. Some researchers see it mainly as a statistical artefact.
L'article de 1999, dans le Journal of Pe: The 1999 paper, in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, is titled "Unskilled and Unaware of It". In 2000 it earned its authors an Ig Nobel Prize.
En 1995 à Pittsburgh, McArthur Wheeler b: In 1995 in Pittsburgh, McArthur Wheeler robbed banks bare-faced, his face smeared with lemon juice. His photo was shown on the 11 pm news on 19 April; he was arrested less than an hour later and protested: "But I wore the lemon juice."
Le psychologue américain John Flavell do: The American psychologist John Flavell named metacognition in 1979. But Aristotle already discussed it in the 4th century BC, in his treatise On the Soul and the Parva Naturalia.
En 1981, Ola Svenson interroge des étudi: In 1981, Ola Svenson surveyed students: 93% of the Americans and 69% of the Swedes put themselves in the top half of drivers. It is also called the "Lake Wobegon" effect, after the fictional town where all the children are above average.
Kahneman et Tversky proposent l'erreur d: Kahneman and Tversky proposed the planning fallacy in 1979. The Sydney Opera House was meant to be finished in 1963 for 7 million dollars; a scaled-down version opened in 1973, for 102 million.
Pauline Clance et Suzanne Imes décrivent: Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes described this "impostor phenomenon" in 1978, in high-achieving women: an inner feeling of intellectual phoniness.
Francis Bacon conseillait déjà cette mét: Francis Bacon already recommended this method in 1620, and William James noted in 1890 that memory retains better through active than passive repetition. The first experimental study was published by Edwina Abbott in 1909.
Emily Pronin, à Princeton, crée l'expres: Emily Pronin, at Princeton, coined the phrase in 2002 with Daniel Lin and Lee Ross. In a survey of more than 600 Americans, over 85% judged themselves less biased than average; only one person judged themselves more biased.
Kahneman et Tversky décrivent l'aversion: Kahneman and Tversky described loss aversion in prospect theory, published in 1979 in Econometrica. This work underpinned Kahneman's 2002 Nobel Prize in economics.
Dans la théorie des perspectives (1979),: In prospect theory (1979), the pain of losing 1,000 dollars is only offset by the pleasure of gaining about 2,000.
On l'appelle aussi « sophisme du Concord: It is also called the "Concorde fallacy": the British and French governments kept funding the supersonic plane long after it was clear it would not pay off.
Richard Thaler nomme l'effet en 1980. Da: Richard Thaler named the effect in 1980. In the 1990 Cornell experiment, students who had been given a mug wanted about 7 dollars for it, while buyers offered only about 3.
Samuelson et Zeckhauser le mettent en év: Samuelson and Zeckhauser demonstrated it with a questionnaire in 1988. In the early 1990s, New Jersey and Pennsylvania inadvertently ran the experiment: drivers mostly kept the default insurance option.
En 2003, Eric Johnson et Daniel Goldstei: In 2003, Eric Johnson and Daniel Goldstein argued that this default rule, presumed consent or consent to be given, is the main cause of the gap in donor rates between countries.
Barry Schwartz publie Le Paradoxe du cho: Barry Schwartz published The Paradox of Choice in 2004. A 2010 meta-analysis of 50 studies, however, found no meaningful link between abundant choice and anxiety.
Les premières inversions de préférence o: The first preference reversals were observed in rats and pigeons, as in George Ainslie's 1974 study on impulse control in pigeons.
Sur le conseil de Circé, Ulysse met de l: On Circe's advice, Ulysses put wax in his sailors' ears and had himself tied to the mast. Some psychiatric advance directives are today called "Ulysses pacts".
Nudge, de Richard Thaler et Cass Sunstei: Nudge, by Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein, came out in 2008. It defends "libertarian paternalism": arranging how choices are presented without banning any. Thaler received the Nobel Prize in economics in 2017.
Ce Nobel 2002 récompense la théorie des: This 2002 Nobel rewarded prospect theory, written with Amos Tversky and published in Econometrica in 1979.
Herbert Simon forge l'expression ; il dé: Herbert Simon coined the phrase; he developed the idea in Models of Man, in 1957. He received the Nobel Prize in economics alone in 1978, and in 1975 the Turing Award with Allen Newell for his work on artificial intelligence.
Edward Simpson le décrit en 1951, mais K: Edward Simpson described it in 1951, but Karl Pearson in 1899 and Udny Yule in 1903 had already noted similar effects. Colin Blyth gave it the name "Simpson's paradox" in 1972.
L'étude de Bickel, Hammel et O'Connell,: The study by Bickel, Hammel and O'Connell, "Sex Bias in Graduate Admissions: Data From Berkeley", was published in 1975 and became the classic example of Simpson's paradox.
Les expressions « sophisme du procureur: The terms "prosecutor's fallacy" and "defense attorney's fallacy" were introduced in 1987 by William Thompson and Edward Schumann.
L'expert, le pédiatre Roy Meadow, sous-e: The expert, the paediatrician Roy Meadow, also underestimated how often such deaths occur. The Royal Statistical Society issued a statement pointing out the errors, and Sally Clark's conviction was quashed on 29 January 2003.
Francis Galton popularise l'idée à la fi: Francis Galton popularised the idea at the end of the 19th century, in 1886, with "Regression towards mediocrity in hereditary stature". Kahneman showed it explains why rebukes seem to work and praise to backfire.
Un sportif arrive en couverture après un: An athlete makes the cover after an exceptional run; their results then drift back toward average, which looks like a curse. Galton had described this regression as early as 1886.
Le mot « p-hacking » est forgé en 2014 p: The word "p-hacking" was coined in 2014 by the three researchers behind the Data Colada blog. In 2015, journalist John Bohannon revealed he had rigged a study on chocolate for weight loss: it took 18 variables to get below p < 0.05.
Darrell Huff le décrit en 1954 dans Comm: Darrell Huff described it in 1954 in How to Lie with Statistics, illustrated by Irving Geis: cutting off the bottom of a chart magnifies differences. It is one of the best-selling statistics books in history.
Le raisonnement vient de Thomas Bayes :: The reasoning comes from Thomas Bayes: his essay, reworked by Richard Price after his death, appeared in 1763. Laplace found the same rule independently in 1774.
Le Literary Digest avait envoyé 10 milli: The Literary Digest had sent out 10 million ballots and got 2.38 million replies, drawn from lists of telephone users and car owners. George Gallup, with only 50,000 people, got it right. The magazine folded in 1938.
Joseph Berkson montre en 1946 qu'étudier: Joseph Berkson showed in 1946 that studying only hospital patients creates false associations between diseases, because people end up in hospital precisely because they are ill.
Des chercheurs parlent d'un « détecteur: Researchers speak of a "hyperactive agent detection device": wrongly imagining a predator behind a snapping twig costs little, while missing a real one can be fatal.
Le cliché de Viking 1 date du 25 juillet: The Viking 1 image dates from 25 July 1976. The sharper images from Mars Global Surveyor led NASA to describe a natural hill whose face-like look depends on the viewing angle.
La maxime paraît en 1980 dans un livre d: The maxim appeared in 1980 in a book by Arthur Bloch on Murphy's law, attributed to a certain Robert J. Hanlon. Robert Heinlein had written in 1941: "You have attributed conditions to villainy that simply result from stupidity."
Gérald Bronner publie La Démocratie des: Gérald Bronner published La Démocratie des crédules in 2013, then Apocalypse cognitive in January 2021. He shows how hoaxes and fake news pile up in layers of arguments.
Une étude a montré que croire que Ben La: One study showed that believing Bin Laden was already dead before his compound in Pakistan was raided makes people more likely to believe… that he is still alive.
Skinner nourrissait des pigeons à interv: Skinner fed pigeons at regular intervals, whatever they did. The birds started repeating "rituals": they behaved, he wrote, as if there were a causal relation between their behaviour and the food.
L'Américaine Dorothy Martin annonçait un: The American Dorothy Martin predicted a flood before dawn on 21 December 1954. Festinger, Riecken and Schachter infiltrated her group, the Seekers, and published When Prophecy Fails in 1956. Archival work has since cast doubt on part of the account.
En 2007, Leman et Cinnirella font lire à: In 2007, Leman and Cinnirella had 64 participants read about the assassination, attempted or successful, of a fictional president: the graver the consequences, the more they believed in a conspiracy.
L'étude de Tuskegee dure de 1932 à 1972: The Tuskegee study ran from 1932 to 1972: 399 Black men with syphilis were left untreated, even after 1947 when penicillin became standard therapy. Whistleblower Peter Buxtun had it exposed by Jean Heller of the Associated Press in July 1972.
James Randi lance son défi en 1964 avec: James Randi launched his challenge in 1964 with 1,000 dollars; a friend, Rick Adams, raised it to a million in 1996. About a thousand people applied, none succeeded, and the challenge ended in 2015.
Le nom vient de Fiona Broome, chercheuse: The name comes from Fiona Broome, a paranormal researcher, who remembered news coverage of Nelson Mandela dying in prison in the 1980s. He died in 2013.
L'idée est ancienne : Hume écrivait en 1: The idea is old: Hume wrote in 1748 that testimony loses force the more unusual the fact, and Laplace that the weight of evidence must be proportioned to the strangeness of the claim. Marcello Truzzi had put it this way in 1978.
Gary Klein décrit la méthode en 2007 dan: Gary Klein described the method in 2007 in the Harvard Business Review: you start from the assumption that "the patient has died". It formalises the "prospective hindsight" studied by Mitchell, Russo and Pennington in 1989.
L'idée vient de Kahneman et Tversky. Ben: The idea comes from Kahneman and Tversky. In 2004 Bent Flyvbjerg turned it into a practical method, reference class forecasting, published in June 2004 by the UK Department for Transport.
Dans le Good Judgment Project de Tetlock: In Tetlock's Good Judgment Project, the best forecasters did about 30% better than the average intelligence analyst with access to secret data. Tetlock told the story in Superforecasting, in 2015, with Dan Gardner.
Philip Tetlock publie ces résultats en 2: Philip Tetlock published these results in 2005 in Expert Political Judgment: experts often predict no better than other people, and are rarely held to account when wrong.
Le théorème de Thomas Bayes paraît en 17: Thomas Bayes's theorem appeared in 1763 after his death, edited by Richard Price. Harold Jeffreys said it is to probability theory what Pythagoras's theorem is to geometry.
Karl Pearson regroupe dès 1904 plusieurs: Karl Pearson pooled several studies on the typhoid vaccine as early as 1904. The word "meta-analysis" was coined in 1976 by the statistician Gene Glass: "the analysis of analyses".
Le mot vient du grec zētētikós, « qui ai: The word comes from the Greek zētētikós, "one who likes to search", a name given to the sceptics who followed Pyrrho. Henri Broch revived it in the 1980s and founded the zetetics laboratory at the University of Nice in 1998.
Cicéron raconte qu'on montra à Diagoras: Cicero tells how Diagoras of Melos was shown the votive paintings of sailors saved from shipwreck. He replied that the pictures of those who drowned were missing, and they were far more numerous.
L'Allemand Karl Kahlbaum introduit le mo: The German Karl Kahlbaum introduced the word in 1866, from the Greek pará, "beside", and eídōlon, "image". Leonardo da Vinci already advised painters to look for scenes in the stains on walls.
